title: Commands, shortcuts and recent files
hints: For `shorten`, try keeping all but the first two parts, then all but the first three, and so on: the first candidate that fits keeps the most.
Compare paths through a lower-case copy, but store and show them exactly as they were added.
requirements: Shortcuts are unique, and only enabled commands are triggered by keys.
Menu lines show the canonical shortcut and the checked and disabled states.
The recent list keeps the newest first, without duplicates in any letter case, and survives saving and loading.
Long paths are shortened from the middle, and ampersands in paths are shown literally.
stretch: Remove recent files that no longer exist when the menu opens (in a real program, `GetFileAttributesW` returning `INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES`), and let the user edit the shortcut table in a dialog, saving it next to the recent files.
